liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (5 reviews): Reportedly the first first-set Dark Star since 1971, played for poster artist Rick Griffin, hospitalized after a motorcycle accident; it goes little distance; Reviewer notes the unusual placement of Dark Star in the first set [13][17][20][21][22]
- **Victim Or The Crime** (3 reviews): Bruce guides the band from Scarlet into Victim and then back out to Fire, interacting closely with Jerry; Bruce clearly leads the band into Victim in the Scarlet > Victim > Fire sequence [11][17][22]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Bruce riffs over everything in Scarlet and starts steering toward Victim around five and a half minutes in; Scarlet is lush and exploratory, then melts into a dissonant Victim [12][13]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Bruce's playing on the Jack Straw and Bertha openers is singled out as stunning [12]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Truckin' contains a long exploratory jam leading into the drums [13]
- **Playin' In The Band Reprise** (1 review): The jam coming out of Space bubbles up into a sweet Playin' reprise, then slows into Standing On the Moon [18]
- **Standing On the Moon** (1 review): Standing On the Moon is the only song reaching 1991's usual standard, per this reviewer [21]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Good Lovin' closes the set with Jerry singing so hard the reviewer feared he'd blow a gasket [18]

## Setlist highlights

- **first set of 91-05-12, untracked**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1991-08-16.sbd.nickc.111330.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 211 min; rated 4/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd91-08-16.sbd.braverman.6676.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 172 min; rated 4.25/5 by 32 [3]. Said about its sound: Phil's bass strings sound loose or off during the first set, giving an odd but interesting tone; Phil's bass has an odd problem during Jack Straw, which the reviewer finds novel and unusual; Reviewer describes the recording as muddy and the playing as sloppy [12][16][21][22]
- **gd91-08-16.sbd.17011.sbeok.flac**: soundboard; 18 songs; 158 min; rated 4.14/5 by 7 [2]
- **gd1991-08-16.141274.sbd.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 17 songs; 161 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer finds this show much more intense than the typical 1991 show [16]
- Reviewer ranks this among the three best 1991 shows, crediting Hornsby with pushing Jerry's playing [19]
- Reviewer disputes it being a top-three show of 1991, finding it less energetic than this lineup's best that year [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1991-08-16.sbd.nickc.111330.flac16**: transferred by nickc; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Source is Nick's soundboard; the uploader credits him for DAT masters and clones made with the uploader's mics and gear; Admin note: the recording was first labeled an audience master, then corrected to a soundboard [1]
- **gd91-08-16.sbd.braverman.6676.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD:DAT> DAT> SF> WAV> SHN [3]
- **gd91-08-16.sbd.17011.sbeok.flac**: source: SB DAT 48khz low-gen clone [2]
- **gd1991-08-16.141274.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Wolfgang's: [Grateful Dead Laminate from Shoreline Amphitheatre, Aug 16, 1991 at Wolfgang's](https://www.wolfgangs.com/backstage-passes/grateful-dead/laminate/SHO910816.html) [24]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1991-08-16 Grateful Dead Ticket - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1991-08-16-grateful-dead-ticket/) [25]
